paper.title: LLM+P: Empowering Large Language Models with Optimal Planning Proficiency
paper.central_claim: LLM+P combines an LLM translator and a classical planner to return correct or optimal long-horizon plans, providing optimal solutions for most benchmark problems where direct LLMs fail even to produce feasible plans, and improving service-robot planning efficiency.

signatures.object: LLM attempting combinatorial action sequencing directly
signatures.information: Natural-language problem, expert-written PDDL domain specifying preconditions/effects, one paired NL/problem-PDDL example; abstracted state rather than online raw sensor grounding.
signatures.operation: Frozen GPT4 translates problem into PDDL; Fast Downward computes a plan; LLM translates returned plan back to language.
signatures.output: Solver-computed formal plan and natural-language rendering.
signatures.conditions: Handwritten domain and generated init/goal facts must faithfully model real task; solver optimality refers to that formal model/cost, not physical semantics.
signatures.feedback: Solver reports feasibility/timeout; no demonstrated iterative LLM repair or closed-loop physical execution-failure replanning.
signatures.selection_rule: Try optimal alias then disclosed feasible fallback;200s search; one temperature0 generated PDDL response.
signatures.data: 7 IPC robot-planning domains ×20 generated tasks, one contextual pair/domain as described; direct-LLM and no-context controls.
signatures.persistence: Fixed domain/example and planner software; no retained library, self-improvement or online parameter updates.
signatures.later_use: New instances reuse domain and example; no learned correction accumulated across problems.
signatures.claimed_effect: More correct/optimal plans than direct GPT4 and ToT; one shorter robot tidy-up route.
signatures.failure_boundary: Missing facts, fake predicates and disconnected states; no solution in Floortile; human formal domain and state abstraction carry competence.

gap.author_gap: LLMs cannot reliably solve long-horizon plans, whereas classical search can solve formally specified planning instances.
gap.checked_gap: Formal problem construction is separable from combinatorial search, but already sits in classical planning/tool-augmentation lineage. The empirical residual is whether a pretrained translator plus example yields solver-usable problem files, not a new optimal planning algorithm.

lineage.method: STRIPS/Shakey, HTN/PRODIGY, PDDL classical planning, LLM direct/CoT/ToT planning and external tool augmentation
lineage.source_version: 2304.11477v3 II/IV/V descriptions; external original versions not independently fixed/read

gap.closest_adjacent: Existing PDDL planners already guarantee model-conditional plan properties; LLM+P adds the natural-language-to-problem front end. Compared with direct language planning, human domain knowledge and formal solver are added together.
gap.residue: Plausible fluent action lists violate preconditions; correct formal models remain expensive and semantically error-prone to construct.
gap.stakes: Infeasible or unnecessarily costly robot plans cannot be rescued by fluency.
gap.method_response: Confine GPT4 to translation with example/domain context and delegate search to Fast Downward.
gap.remaining_gap: No sound semantic translation, automated domain discovery, general method-trigger detection, execution-failure repair or repeated robot reliability; majority-optimal headline not supported by Table I as equally weighted140 tasks.
unresolved: External novelty/first-framework claim not independently verified.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E02 (ablation, common_practice).** Attribute a gain to a harness component only through one-at-a-time toggles (leave-one-out or single add) with the backbone fixed. A cumulative stack (A, then +B, then +C) or a bundle-level comparison does not separate components or their interactions. — _applies when_ a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E04 (reproducibility, common_practice).** Report run-to-run variance and use paired task-level statistics: repeated runs per setting, bootstrap or permutation CIs over tasks, and sign tests on discordant episodes. A single run on a 100-episode subset is treated as descriptive. In the read single-run papers, differences of a few points sit within noise. — _applies when_ any success-rate comparison between harnesses, models or training recipes on a fixed task subset.
expectations.applies_when: any success-rate comparison between harnesses, models or training recipes on a fixed task subset.

claims.text: Optimal solutions for most benchmark problems.
claims.setting: 140 generated tasks in7 IPC robot-planning domains, GPT4 temp0,200s search
claims.baseline/control: Same GPT4 direct with/without example, ToT, LLM+P with/without PDDL context; expert formal domain remains additional structure
claims.data_budget: 20 tasks/domain; one deterministic PDDL response; optimal seq-opt-fdss-1 with lama feasible fallback
claims.selection_vs_test: Example drawn from same domain family; held-out generated instances but no excluded-domain/template split or pretraining audit
claims.result: Optimal rates20,90,0,95,85,20,10%; equal20 denominators yield64/140=45.7%, not majority. Including displayed feasible fallback rates yields97/140=69.3%, a different claim.
claims.denominator: 7×20=140 formal instances, one response each; our arithmetic from author's Table I, not a reproduction
claims.counterevidence: Floortile0, Termes20 and Tyreworld10 optimal; translation failures. Parenthesized100/100/90 fallback rows are feasible, not necessarily optimal.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Formal planning substantially improves feasible/optimal instance outcomes vs direct LLM in several domains; majority-optimal across all140 is not substantiated by Table I.

claims.setting: One tidy-up scenario with explicit distances, one gripper and supplied symbolic state
claims.data_budget: One demonstrated scenario, no repeated execution-success study
claims.selection_vs_test: Illustrative construction; no independent physical holdout
claims.result: Shorter formal route under supplied model/cost, shown on robot
claims.denominator: One illustrated task; no repeated physical trial n
claims.counterevidence: Metric is modeled route cost, not measured runtime or general task reliability; human/domain/state assumptions unchanged.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A model-conditional cost advantage can be instantiated in a robot example; not broad closed-loop efficient robot transfer.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Scope-B robot-planning harness: author-reported GPT4 PDDL translation plus Fast Downward improves model-conditional formal plan success over direct language planning on several domains. One robot demonstration illustrates route-cost benefit; no repeated closed-loop robot evaluation. Table I supports45.7% optimal across140 equally weighted tasks, not majority-optimal.
unresolved: Majority-optimal abstract/findings wording conflicts with Table I arithmetic unless a narrower successful-subset denominator is specified; preserve original claim rather than silently repair it.
Human-written domain and full symbolic state do not guarantee natural-language semantics or real-world validity.
No solver-feedback semantic repair or physical failure-replanning experiment.
No repeated robot trial denominator or total inference/human-modeling cost.
No formal transfer label granted merely for multiple symbolic domains and one robot demo.

G.reason: Important precondition/reasoning bottleneck and translator/search seam clearly located in classical planning lineage; first-framework priority and adjacent originals not independently verified.

M.reason: Delegating search directly addresses long-horizon sequencing and gives model-conditional optimality, but semantic translation and human domain assumptions prevent guarantees about original task.

X.reason: PDDL/context→solver→language flow, aliases, fallback and timeout reconstructable; no invented repair/persistence, but errors remain unchecked at semantic/physical boundary.

measurement.reason: Explicit formal criterion,140-instance denominator and optimal/feasible distinction; all deterministic one-pass outcomes and single robot illustration imply anchors-v2 measurement ceiling2. Majority-optimal arithmetic weakens headline, not all observed gains.

causality.reason: Same-model direct/no-context/ToT comparisons show system utility, but expert domain, intermediate representation and solver jointly change; no semantic-validation isolation or matched total compute.

holdout.reason: Multiple domain families and generated instances extend coverage, but examples/domain knowledge shared within family, no untouched domain/template construction holdout and no counted real transfer.

statistics.reason: Per-domain20-instance rates and translation failure categories exist, but a single temperature0 response and one robot example lack repeat uncertainty/paired tests; narrow descriptive statistical evidence.

cost.reason: 200s search cap also applied to ToT; formal robot route objective reported separately. Total GPT tokens/latency and manual modeling not priced, so incomplete budget fairness.
